speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've had these skin lesions and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions distributed in a linear or dermatomal pattern, and do they appear to be fluid-filled vesicles? Have you noticed any fever or changes in the child's general behavior or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those characteristics are classic for Molluscum contagiosum, especially given the daycare exposure. I will confirm the diagnosis by examining the lesions closely for the central umbilication. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the additional history. Given the classic presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules and the daycare exposure, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
